Background knowledge

Scenario

Theory & Technique


BPTT (gradient explode) → TBPTT (no consider the future value) → SHAC


Short Horizon Actor-Critic (SHAC)
Actor
\mathcal{L}_{\theta} = -\frac{1}{Nh} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \left[ \left( \sum_{t=t_0}^{t_0+h-1} \gamma^{t-t_0} \mathcal{R}(\mathbf{s}_t^i, \mathbf{a}_t^i) \right) + \gamma^h V_\phi(\mathbf{s}_{t_0+h}^i) \right]
Critic
\mathcal{L}_{\phi} = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{s} \in \{\tau_i\}} \left[ \Vert{} V_{\phi}(\mathbf{s}) - \tilde{V}(\mathbf{s}) \Vert{}^2 \right]
\tilde{V}(\mathbf{s}_t) = (1 - \lambda) \left( \sum_{k=1}^{h-t-1} \lambda^{k-1} G_t^k \right) + \lambda^{h-t-1} G_t^{h-t},
G_t^k = \left( \sum_{l=0}^{k-1} \gamma^l r_{t+l} \right) + \gamma^k V_\phi(\mathbf{s}_{t+k})


\mathcal{L}_{\theta} update
Calculate the adjoint from the last step in reverse order, we assume h = 32, t_0 = 0, i  represents the i th trajectory
  
  💡
計算出每一個時刻(t)的\frac{\partial\mathcal{L_\theta}}{\partial a_t} → 可以求出\frac{\partial\mathcal{L_\theta}}{\partial \theta}
  

Loss function for actor

\mathcal{L}_{\theta} = -\frac{1}{Nh} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \left[ \left( \sum_{t=t_0}^{t_0+h-1} \gamma^{t-t_0} \mathcal{R}(\mathbf{s}_t^i, \mathbf{a}_t^i) \right) + \gamma^h V_\phi(\mathbf{s}_{t_0+h}^i) \right]


Terminal gradient t = 32 = t_0+h
\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_\theta}{\partial \mathbf{s}^i_{t_0+h}} = -\gamma^h \frac{1}{Nh} \frac{\partial V_\theta(\mathbf{s}^i_{t_0+h})}{\partial \mathbf{s}^i_{t_0+h}} \tag{9} 


Calculate \frac{\partial\mathcal{L_\theta}}{\partial a_t} and \frac{\partial\mathcal{L_\theta}}{\partial s_t} in  0 \le t < 32, from t = 31.
\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_\theta}{\partial \mathbf{s}^i_t} = -\gamma^{t-t_0} \frac{1}{Nh} \frac{\partial \mathcal{R}(\mathbf{s}^i_t, \mathbf{a}^i_t)}{\partial \mathbf{s}^i_t} + \left(\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_\theta}{\partial \mathbf{s}^i_{t+1}}\right) \left( \left(\frac{\partial \mathcal{F}}{\partial \mathbf{s}^i_t}\right) + \left(\frac{\partial \mathcal{F}}{\partial \mathbf{a}^i_t}\right)\left(\frac{\partial \pi_\theta(\mathbf{s}^i_t)}{\partial \mathbf{s}^i_t}\right) \right) \tag{10} 
\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_\theta}{\partial \mathbf{a}^i_t} = -\gamma^{t-t_0} \frac{1}{Nh} \frac{\partial \mathcal{R}(\mathbf{s}^i_t, \mathbf{a}^i_t)}{\partial \mathbf{a}^i_t} + \left(\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_\theta}{\partial \mathbf{s}^i_{t+1}}\right) \left(\frac{\partial \mathcal{F}}{\partial \mathbf{a}^i_t}\right) \tag{11}
 
 💡
(9) 可以帶入 (10), \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_\theta}{\partial \mathbf{s}^i_{32}}  → \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_\theta}{\partial \mathbf{s}^i_{31}}
(9) 可以帶入 (11), \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_\theta}{\partial \mathbf{s}^i_{32}}  → \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_\theta}{\partial \mathbf{a}^i_{31}}
以此類推，迭代得到
\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_\theta}{\partial \mathbf{a}^i_{31}}, \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_\theta}{\partial \mathbf{a}^i_{30}}, \cdots , \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_\theta}{\partial \mathbf{a}^i_{0}}  
 


Derive  \frac{\partial\mathcal{L_\theta}}{\partial \theta}
\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_\theta}{\partial \theta} = \sum_{i=1}^{N} \sum_{t=t_0}^{t_0+h-1} \left(\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_\theta}{\partial \mathbf{a}^i_t}\right) \left(\frac{\partial \pi_\theta(\mathbf{s}^i_t)}{\partial \theta}\right) \tag{12}
Update \theta with ADAM

www.youtube.com/watch
Scenario
Dynamically manipulation for large and heavy objects with whole-body dexterity.

Whole-body loco-manipulation while walking, pushing, dragging, lifting, or using body contacts.
Example tasks include uprighting a 15 kg tire, stacking tires, dragging a barrier, pushing a 20 kg box, opening a door, and pushing a table.


Problem Statement

End-to-end RL is robust, BUT

New tasks adaptation: reward redesign, retraining, and expensive tuning


Sample-based MPC is flexible and training-free for contact-rich manipulation, BUT

Curse of dimensionality
Unstable single-shooting rollouts


Core problem

How to adapt to unseen objects without task-specific retraining, while preserving whole-body stability (def of unseen is discussed later)


Test-time steerable generalist whole-body control policy

NO teleoperation references
NO fixed contact modes
NO task-specific motion libraries.
Goal-conditioned (via costs & constraints) loco-manipulation



Contributions


Proposes Sumo, a hierarchical framework combining:

High-level sample-based MPC: reasons contacts and plans the robot-object interactive movements
Low-level RL whole-body control policy: whole-body movements execution + stabilization
Hybrid RL-MPC: the MPC steers the pre-trained RL policy effectively for contact-rich loco-manipulation tasks.



Address key shortcomings of both: HOW?

MPC: plans in the command space of RL policy (reduced search/decision space), more effective.
RL: steered at test-time and can adapt without task-specific retraining.



Robust, flexible, and generalizes to unseen objects

Keeping high-level decision making (steering by costs)
Flexibly adjusting the cost function at test time without tuning or training.

  
  📌
Assumption Definition of the generalization to unseen objects
Reusing the same controller on new objects and new task objectives by changing only the planner’s object model (3D mesh, pose, collision, and inertia info, etc.) or cost function at test time, without retraining.
  


Demonstrates 8 real-world Spot tasks and 4 simulated G1 humanoid tasks, along with benchmark/dataset/code.




How Sumo Combines the Best of RL and MPC
The key idea is to let MPC optimize over the command space of a pre-trained RL whole-body policy, rather than directly optimizing joint-level commands.
a_{t:t+T}^{*} = \arg\min J(s_{t:t+T}, a_{t:t+T})
The MPC action a is not sent directly to the robot as joint commands. Instead, it is passed to the RL whole-body policy:
u_t = \pi_{\text{RL}}(s_t, a_t)
So the rollout dynamics become:
s_{t+1} = f(s_t, \pi_{\text{RL}}(s_t, a_t))
This means MPC searches over a smaller and more stable high-level action space, such as base velocity, arm targets, torso targets, leg selection, and gripper commands. The RL policy handles whole-body stabilization and locomotion, while MPC handles online task reasoning and object interaction.
Real-time cost steering


Takeaway
Sumo uses RL for what RL is good at — robust whole-body locomotion and stabilization — and MPC for what MPC is good at — online task reasoning, object-model adaptation, and cost-function flexibility.
Limitations

Strong assumption on perception completeness

Whole-body contact & object interaction reasoning rely on accurate perception of object and reset in MuJoCo sim in real-time.
MoCap is used instead in this paper. While practically object pose estimation can not easily achieve this level of real-time performance
This is the bottleneck.

Encapsulation is the bundling of data (attributes) and methods (functions) that operate on that data into a single unit called a class. It also involves restricting direct access to some of an object’s components, which helps protect the integrity of the data.

Abstraction is the concept of hiding complex implementation details and showing only the essential features of an object. It allows programmers to focus on what an object does rather than how it does it, typically achieved through abstract classes and interfaces.

Inheritance is a mechanism where a new class (derived or child class) inherits properties and behaviors from an existing class (base or parent class). This promotes code reusability and establishes a hierarchical relationship between classes.

While these three models are mathematically equivalent (providing the same equations of motion), they offer different perspectives—focusing on forces, energies, or state-space trajectories.
1.
Newtonian Model

Core Perspective: Based on Forces and Vector Balance.


**Key Equation**: $F = m\ddot{q}$.



In Simulation: Often extended to the Newton-Euler equations to account for rotation:
M(q)\ddot{q} + C(q, \dot{q}) = \tau
(Where M is the mass matrix, C accounts for Coriolis/gravity/centrifugal forces, and \tau is the generalized force).



**Usage**: Ideal for simulating rigid-body systems and handling contact impulses.

2.
Lagrangian Model

Core Perspective: Based on Energy and the Principle of Least Action.


**Key Equation**: Defines the Lagrangian as $\mathcal{L} = T - V$ (Kinetic - Potential Energy). The motion follows the **Euler-Lagrange Equation**:

$$\frac{d}{dt} \left( \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial \dot{q}} \right) - \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial q} = 0$$

-
**Usage**: Frequently used because it handles **generalized coordinates** (like joint angles) naturally, effectively eliminating internal constraint forces.

3.
Hamiltonian Model

Core Perspective: Based on Total Energy and Conservation Laws.
Key Equation: Uses the Hamiltonian H = T + V (Total Energy). It converts second-order equations into two first-order equations involving position (q) and momentum (p).


**Usage**: Used in simulators (like **Dojo**) to ensure **conservation of momentum and energy**, providing high numerical stability even with large time steps.

Techniques/Machine-Learning/Flow-Matchin.title: Flow Matching
Techniques/Machine-Learning/Flow-Matchin.content:
Training Procedure
Step 1: Sample Expert Trajectory and Noise


Expert action trajectory:

x_1 = [a_1, a_2, \dots, a_H] \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times d}



Noise trajectory:
x_0 \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I) \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times d} 


H:  action steps
d : action dimension, i.e, a 6-axis robot arm has d = 6 for joint position (q)

💡
If there are 50 (H=50) action steps, the noise should also be 50, and the noise will gradually flow to the actual trajectory in a vector field.


Step 2: Sample Flow Time and Construct Interpolation Path


Sample a scalar:
t \sim \mathcal{U}(0, 1) 


Construct an interpolation trajectory:
x(t) = (1 - t)x_0 + t x_1 


This defines a reference path in trajectory space from noise to expert data.

Step 3: Compute Ground-Truth Velocity
Since the interpolation path is predefined, its time derivative is:
\dot{x}(t) = x_1 - x_0 
This velocity serves as the supervision signal.

Step 4: Train Neural Network to Match the Velocity Field
Train a neural network v_\theta(x(t), t, c) to predict the velocity:
v_\theta(x(t), t, c) \approx x_1 - x_0

Loss function:
\mathcal{L}
= \mathbb{E}_{x_0, x_1, t}
\left[
\|v_\theta(x(t), t, c) - (x_1 - x_0)\|^2
\right]
c:  conditioning information (state, vision, language)

💡

在訓練時，針對同一個ground truth trajectory x_1, 會sample 很多noise x_0 ，所以在vector field 上每一個 x_0 跟 x_1 會學到一小部份vector, 很多 x_0 就建立一張完整的 vector field 了
robot 在移動時每一個時刻都會有不同的 x_1, 所以會有很多不同的vector field ，這些vector field 會根據 condition (c) 來改變。



Graph Illustration

Purple dotted line: interpolation path
Purple solid line: ground truth velocity
Inference Procedure
The velocity of the current state is the distance between x_0 and x_1, so we can say the after the update of state, by newton euler integration
x_{t+\Delta t} = x_t + v_\theta(x_t, t, c) \cdot \Delta t
x_t: current state at time t
v_\theta(x_t, t, c): predicted velocity from the neural network
\Delta t: integration step size, depends on how much step you want to do, i.e, If step number = N, the \Delta t = \frac{1}{N}
x_{t+\Delta t}: next state after integration

💡

如果 \Delta t = 1 , 那就是  1 步到目標，但通常會跑 5- 10 步 (N=5-10)，因為 v_\theta(x_t, t, c) 所估出來的值不會是完全準確的

Purple trajectory: the ideal action state after 5 updates
Orange trajectory: the true action state update after 5 updates, due to the training error between v_\theta and \dot x

derivative:

Techniques/Mathematics/Statistics/統計推斷核心.title: 統計推斷核心：MLE 與 Fisher Information
Techniques/Mathematics/Statistics/統計推斷核心.content:
Log Likelihood
似然函數衡量在給定參數 \theta 下，觀測到數據 X = \{x_1, \dots, x_n\} 的可能性。

定義 (Likelihood): L(\theta) = \prod_{i=1}^{n} P(x_i | \theta)
定義 (Log Likelihood): \ell(\theta) = \log L(\theta) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \log P(x_i | \theta)💡 為什麼使用 Log?


計算簡化：將相乘變為相加，方便求導。
數值穩定：避免多個機率相乘導致的數值下溢（Underflow）。
單調性：不改變極值點的位置。

Score Function
對數似然函數對參數的一階導數。
• 定義:s(\theta) = \nabla_\theta \ell(\theta) = \frac{\partial \log L(\theta)}{\partial \theta}
• 物理意義: 表示似然函數在 \theta 處的「斜率」與「方向」。
• 性質:
◦ 在 MLE 估計值處，s(\hat{\theta}_{MLE}) = 0。
◦ 期望值: E[s(\theta)] = 0。
Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE)
一種估計模型參數的準則。
• 核心思想: 尋找一個 \theta 使得觀測數據出現的機率最大化。
• 數學表示:\hat{\theta}_{MLE} = \arg\max_{\theta} \ell(\theta)
• 求解步驟:
1. 列出對數似然函數 \ell(\theta)。
2. 求對 \theta的一階導數（Score Function）。
3. 令 s(\theta) = 0 並解方程。
4. 檢查二階導數（Hessian）是否小於 0（確認為極大值）。
Fisher Information Matrix (費雪信息矩陣)
衡量數據中包含關於參數 \theta 的「資訊量」。
• 定義 (矩陣形式):I(\theta) = E \left[ s(\theta) s(\theta)^T \right] = -E \left[ \frac{\partial^2 \ell(\theta)}{\partial \theta \partial \theta^T} \right]
• 關鍵理解:
◦ 曲率相關: 它是對數似然函數的「二階導負數的期望值」。
◦ 直觀意義:
▪ 若 I(\theta) 越大 → 似然曲線越尖銳 → 參數估計越精確。
▪ 若 I(\theta) 越小 → 似然曲線越平緩 → 參數估計的不確定性越高。
• Cramér-Rao Lower Bound: 任何無偏估計量的變異數，其下限為 Fisher Information 的倒數 Var(\hat{\theta}) \ge \frac{1}{I(\theta)}。
總結關係圖概念數學表達角色

Basic Probability Concept


Basic definition
\begin{align}
p(X=x) = P[X=x] = P_X(x)
\end{align}
 
 💡 $p(X=x)$ is used in this textbook. **R.V. distribution** and **probability of event** is mixed !!!
 


Bayes rule
\begin{align}
p(x|y) = \frac{p(y|x)p(x)}{p(y)} = \frac{f_{Y|X}(y|x)f_X(x)}{f_Y(y)}
\end{align}
 
 💡 **R.V. distribution‘s** bayes rule
 
\begin{align}
p(x|y,z) = \frac{p(y|x,z)p(x|z)}{p(y|z)} 
\end{align}


proof:
\begin{align}
p(x|y,z) 
& = \frac{p(y,z|x)p(x)}{p(y,z)} \\
& = \frac{p(y,z,x)}{p(y,z)} \\
& = \frac{p(y|z,x)p(z,x)}{p(y|z)p(z)} \\
& = \frac{p(y|z,x)p(x|z)p(z)}{p(y|z)p(z)} \\
& = \frac{p(y|x,z)p(x|z)}{p(y|z)}\\ 

\end{align}


 
 💡 **Bayes rule** constructs the basic structure of the **Bayes filter**
 


Theorem of total probability
if y \in  event space, then the following equations established
\begin{align}
& p(x) = \sum_y{p(x|y)p(y)} \\
& p(x) = \int{p(x|y)p(y)}dy
\end{align}


Robot Environment Interaction


Robot States
\begin{align}
x_{t_1:t_2}=x_{t_1},x_{t_1+1},x_{t_1+2},...,x_{t_2}
\end{align}

Complete state v.s. Incomplete state


Complete: the best predictor of the future
x_t 包含了過去的所有訊息(x_{t_0:t-1},u_{t_0:t-1},z_{t_0:t-1})，已經足夠來預測未來的狀態(state) → 符合 Markov chains


Incomplete: any state is not included in the Complete state.






Measurement data
\begin{align}
z_{t_1:t_2}=z_{t_1},z_{t_1+1},z_{t_1+2},...,z_{t_2}
\end{align}


Control data
\begin{align}
u_{t_1:t_2}=u_{t_1},u_{t_1+1},u_{t_1+2},...,u_{t_2}
\end{align}


Probabilistic Generative Laws
Robots’ states at time t(x_t) is governed by the following equation :
\begin{align}
p(x_t|x_{0:t-1},z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})
\end{align}

💡 透過過去的(states, measurements, controls), 來估計目前狀態($x_t$)的機率分布

By applying Markov chain
\begin{align}
& p(x_t|x_{0:t-1},z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t-1}) \quad & \Rightarrow\quad 
&p(x_t|x_{t-1},u_{t}) \\
& p(z_t|x_{0:t},z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})  \quad & \Rightarrow \quad & p(z_t|x_{t})
\end{align}
Define
p(x_t|x_{t-1},u_{t}) :=  state transition probability
p(z_t|x_{t}):= measurement probability

💡 ***state transition probability*** 和 ***measurement probability*** 可以用來完整描述機器人的以及環境的動態

Belief
Belief means the states that is inferred by the robot from datas
\begin{align}
& bel(x_t) \quad & \Rightarrow\quad 
&p(x_t|z_{1:t},u_{1:t}) \\
&  \bar{bel}(x_t) \quad & \Rightarrow \quad &p(x_t|z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})
\end{align}

💡 **belief** 表示從資料(measurements, controls)中算出的狀態(state)



x_t, u_t,z_t evolution relationship:



Bayes Filters
Bayes Filters is an algorithm to calculate the belief from measurement(z_t) and control data(u_t)


Pseudocode
\begin{align*}
& Bayes\_filter(bel(x_{t−1}), u_t, z_t): \\
& \quad for \ all \ x_t : \\
& \quad \quad \bar{bel}(xt) =\int
p(x_t | u_t, x_{t−1}) bel(x_{t−1}) dx_{t−1} \\
& \quad \quad bel(xt) = η p(z_t | x_t) \bar{bel}(x_t)\\
& \quad endfor \\
& \quad return \ bel(x_t)
\end{align*}

proof:

Two assumptions

state (x_t) is complete
controls (u_t) is chosen randomly (?)





Apply Bayes rule to the target posterior(bel(x_t))
\begin{align}
bel(x_t)
& =p(x_t|z_{1:t},u_{1:t})=\frac{p(z_t|x_t,z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})p(x_t|z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})}{\underbrace{p(z_t|z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})}_{\frac{1}{\eta}}} \\
& = \eta\cdot p(z_t|x_t,z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})p(x_t|z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})
\end{align}


With the assumption x_t is complete, the following equations are established
\begin{align}
& bel(x_t)
=p(x_t|z_{1:t},u_{1:t})= \eta\cdot \underbrace{p(z_t|x_t,z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})}_{p(z_t|x_t)}\underbrace{p(x_t|z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})}_{\bar{bel}(x_t)} \\
& bel(x_t) = \eta \cdot p(z_t|x_t)\bar{bel}(x_t)
\end{align}


By the Theorem of total probability, \bar{bel}(x_t) can be expanded as follow
\begin{align}
\bar{bel}(x_t)
& =p(x_t|z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t}) \\
& =\int{p(x_t|x_{t-1},z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})p(x_{t-1}|z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})}dx_{t-1}
\end{align}


Again, with the assumption x_t is complete, the following equations are established
\begin{align}
\bar{bel}(x_t)

& =\int{\underbrace{p(x_t|x_{t-1},z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})}_{p(x_t|x_{t-1},u_t)}p(x_{t-1}|z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})}dx_{t-1} \\
& = \int p(x_t|x_{t-1},u_t)p(x_{t-1}|z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})dx_{t-1}
\end{align}


with the assumption controls (u_t) is chosen randomly u_t can be omitted.(?)
\begin{align}
\bar{bel}(x_t)
& = \int p(x_t|x_{t-1},u_t)p(x_{t-1}|z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})dx_{t-1} \\
& = \int p(x_t|x_{t-1},u_t)\underbrace{p(x_{t-1}|z_{1:t-1},u_{1:t-1})}_{bel(x_{t-1})}dx_{t-1} \\
& = \int p(x_t|x_{t-1},u_t)bel(x_{t-1})dx_{t-1}
\end{align}


Finally, we obtain the Bayes Filters algorithm
\begin{align}
\begin{align*}
& \bar{bel}(x_t) = \int p(x_t|x_{t-1},u_t)bel(x_{t-1})dx_{t-1} \\
& bel(x_t) = \eta \cdot p(z_t|x_t)\bar{bel}(x_t) \\
\end{align*}
\end{align}






This algorithm requires three probability distributions

p(x_t|x_{t-1},u_{t}) → state transition probability
p(z_t|x_{t}) → measurement probability
p(x_0) → initial belief

Kalman filter is a type of state observer

Kalman filter vs state observer


discrete state observer
\begin{align*}
& \hat{x}_k=A\hat{x}_{k-1}+Bu_{k-1}+K(y_{k-1}-C\hat{x}_{k-1})
\end{align*}


discrete Kalman filter
\begin{align*}
& \hat{x}_k=A\hat{x}_{k-1}+Bu_k+K_k(y_k-C(A\hat{x}_{k-1}+Bu_k))
\end{align*}




Kalman filter derivation
\hat{x}_k^- :=  Priori Estimate( predicted state estimate)
\hat{x}_k :=  Posteriori Estimate
\begin{align*}
& \hat{x}_k=\underbrace{A\hat{x}_{k-1}+Bu_k}_{\hat{x}_k^-}+K_k(y_k-C(\underbrace{A\hat{x}_{k-1}+Bu_k}_{\hat{x}_k^-})) \\
&
\hat{x}_k=\underbrace{\hat{x}_k^-}_{predict}+\underbrace{K_k(y_k-C\hat{x}_k^-)}_{update} \\
\end{align*}
  
  💡 We can simplify the problem to how to get the best $K_k$
  


Kalman filter is a two-step process(with initialization)
Initialization
\hat{x}_0,Q,R,P_0

Remarks

Q, R can be obtained from Statistics
P_0 can be assigned randomly, and it will converge at last
How to choose states (x) is pretty important



Prediction
\begin{align*}
& \hat{x}_k^- = A\hat{x}_{k-1}+Bu_k \\
& P_k^- = AP_{k-1}A^T+Q
\end{align*}
Update
\begin{align*}
& K_k = \frac{P_k^-C^T}{CP_k^-C^T+R} \\
& \hat{x}_k=\hat{x}_k^-+K_k(y_k-C\hat{x}^-_k) \\
& P_k = (I-K_kC)P_k^-
\end{align*}

Notations

Q: Covariance matrix of estimation process noise
R: Covariance matrix of measurement noise
P: Covariance matrix of estimation state
K:Kalman gain

weight update induction :
J(\mathbf{w}) = \mathbb{E}_{\pi}[(v_{\pi}(S) - \hat{v}(S, \mathbf{w}))^{2}]
\begin{aligned} \Delta \mathbf{w} &= -\frac{1}{2} \alpha \nabla_{\mathbf{w}} J(\mathbf{w}) \\ &= \alpha \mathbb{E}_{\pi}[(v_{\pi}(S) - \hat{v}(S, \mathbf{w})) \nabla_{\mathbf{w}} \hat{v}(S, \mathbf{w})] \end{aligned}

value function by a linear combination of features

loss function

\Delta \mathbf{w}

How to measure the quality of  π_\theta(s, a)  ? → How do we define how best \theta  is?


Episodic environments: start value
J(\theta) = V^{\pi_\theta}(s_1) = \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta}[v_1]


Continuing environments
average value
J(\theta) = \sum_{s} d^{\pi_\theta}(s) V^{\pi_\theta}(s)
Average Reward per time-step
J(\theta) = \sum_{s} d^{\pi_\theta}(s) \sum_{a} \pi_\theta(s, a) R_s^a

d^{\pi_\theta}(s): 在 \pi_\theta 這個policy 下，平均停留在 state s 的機率
\sum_{a} \pi_\theta(s, a) R_s^a: 在 \pi_\theta 這個policy下，這個state s 獲得Reward的期望值

  
  💡
如果action 跟 state 是連續的，公式應該改成積分式, e.g.
J_{avR}(\theta) = \int_{S} d^{\pi_\theta}(s) \int_{A} \pi_\theta(a|s) R_s^a \, da \, ds
  




Goal: Find \theta that maximizes J(\theta)
\theta_{new} = \theta_{old} + \Delta\theta 
\Delta\theta = \alpha \nabla_\theta J(\theta)
\nabla_\theta J(\theta) = \begin{bmatrix}
  \frac{\partial J(\theta)}{\partial \theta_1} \
  \cdots \
  \frac{\partial J(\theta)}{\partial \theta_n}
  \end{bmatrix}^\top: policy gradient
Goal:  Compute \nabla_\theta J(\theta) → compute the \nabla_\theta \pi_\theta(s, a)
Goal:  Compute the \nabla_\theta \pi_\theta(s, a)
\begin{aligned}
\nabla_\theta \pi_\theta(s, a) &= \pi_\theta(s, a) \frac{\nabla_\theta \pi_\theta(s, a)}{\pi_\theta(s, a)} \\
&= \pi_\theta(s, a) \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(s, a)
\end{aligned}


score function derivation
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\nabla_\theta \pi_\theta(s, a)}{\pi_\theta(s, a)} & = 
\frac{1}{\pi_\theta(s,a)} \cdot \frac{d\pi_\theta(s,a)}{d\theta} \\&= \frac{d \log \pi_\theta(s,a)}{d\pi_\theta(s,a)} \cdot \frac{d\pi_\theta(s,a)}{d\theta} \\
&= \frac{d \log \pi_\theta(s,a)}{d\theta} \\
&= \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(s, a)
\end{aligned}


\nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(s, a): score function, the gradient of the log-likelihood function
  
  💡
\pi_\theta(s, a): likelihood function, the case that sample number n = 1
  
  
  💡
\nabla_\theta \pi_\theta(s, a): 可以被auto diff 等方法算出，但是之後要算\nabla_\theta J(\theta) 會需要每個state 的R^a_s，但我們沒辦法得到每一個state的R^a_s(太複雜無法遍歷)，我們希望得到期望值的形式(機率x數值)，這樣就可以用sampling 來更新參數
  
Goal:  Compute the score function \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(s, a)
Discrete action space: Softmax policy
\pi_{\theta}(s, a) = \frac{e^{\phi(s, a)^T \theta}}{\sum_{a' \in A} e^{\phi(s, a')^T \theta}}
  
  💡
A 是finite action set. update \theta 等於是udpate 每一個action a 出現的機率
  
Score function
\nabla_{\theta} \log \pi_{\theta}(s, a) = \phi(s, a) - \mathbb{E}_{\pi_{\theta}}[\phi(s, \cdot)]


score function derivation
Take the log of \pi_\theta(s,a)
\log \pi_{\theta}(s, a) = \phi(s, a)^T \theta - \log \sum_{a'} e^{\phi(s, a')^T \theta}
  
  💡
\log(\frac{A}{B}) = \log A - \log B
  
Take the gradient
\nabla_{\theta} \log \pi_{\theta}(s, a) =  \nabla_{\theta} (\phi(s, a)^T \theta) - \nabla_{\theta} \log \sum_{a'} e^{\phi(s, a')^T \theta}

The first term

 \nabla_{\theta} (\phi(s, a)^T \theta) = \phi(s, a)

The second term

\begin{aligned}
\nabla_{\theta} \log \sum_{a'} e^{\phi(s, a')^T \theta} & = \frac{\sum_{a'} e^{\phi(s, a')^T \theta} \cdot \phi(s, a')}{\sum_{a''} e^{\phi(s, a'')^T \theta}} \\
& = \sum_{a'} \left( \frac{e^{\phi(s, a')^T \theta}}{\sum_{a''} e^{\phi(s, a'')^T \theta}} \right) \phi(s, a') \\ 
& = \sum_{a'} \pi_{\theta}(s, a') \phi(s, a') \\
& = \mathbb{E}_{\pi_{\theta}}[\phi(s, \cdot)]
\end{aligned}
Score function
\nabla_{\theta} \log \pi_{\theta}(s, a) = \phi(s, a) - \mathbb{E}_{\pi_{\theta}}[\phi(s, \cdot)]
  
  💡
score function = current feature vector - feature vector expectation
  


Continuous action space: Gaussian policy
Mean: \mu(s) = \phi(s)^\top \theta
Variance: \sigma^2 (assume fixed number)
\pi_\theta(s, a) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2}} \exp \left( -\frac{(a - \phi(s)^\top \theta)^2}{2\sigma^2} \right)
Score function
\nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(s, a) = \frac{(a - \mu(s))\phi(s)}{\sigma^2}
  
  💡
直觀的說 (a - \mu(s)) 決定了參數 \theta 更新的幅度
  


score function derivation
TBD


Caculate the policy gradient \nabla_\theta J(\theta)


Policy gradient for one-step MDP
We try to maximize the estimation of total reward J(\theta)
\begin{aligned}
J(\theta) & = \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta}[r] \\ & = \sum_{s \in S} d(s) \sum_{a \in A} \textcolor{red}{\pi_\theta(s, a) }R_{s,a} \\\nabla_\theta J(\theta) & = \sum_{s \in S} d(s) \sum_{a \in A} \textcolor{red}{\pi_\theta(s, a) \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(s, a)} R_{s,a} \\ & = \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta}[\nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(s, a) r]
\end{aligned}
Gradient ascent
\theta_{t+1} = \theta_t+\alpha \nabla_\theta J(\theta_t)
  
  💡
policy gradient: depends on discrete or continuous → anyway, we can obtain it.
r: reward can be obtained after one step.
→ Traditional update weighting techniques in ML can be applied (e.g. SGD, ADAM…)
  


Policy gradient for multi-step MDP → introduce policy gradient theorem
We try to maximize the estimation of total reward J(\theta)
trajectory \tau = (s_0, a_1, s_1, a_2, \dots, s_T)
trajectory total reward r(\tau)
\begin{aligned}
J(\theta) & = \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta} [r(\tau)] \\
& = \int \pi_\theta(\tau) r(\tau) d\tau
\end{aligned}
\begin{aligned}
\nabla_\theta J(\theta) & = \nabla_\theta \int \pi_\theta(\tau) r(\tau) d\tau \\
& = \int \textcolor{red}{\nabla_\theta \pi_\theta(\tau)} r(\tau) d\tau \\
& = \int \textcolor{red}{\pi_\theta(\tau) \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(\tau)} r(\tau) d\tau \\
& = \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta} [ r(\tau) \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(\tau)]
\end{aligned}
How to get \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(\tau) ?
\pi_\theta(\tau) = \underbrace{P(s_0)}_{\text{1. 初始狀態機率}} \times \underbrace{\prod_{t=1}^T \pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t)}_{\text{2. 策略大腦的選擇 (連乘)}} \times \underbrace{\prod_{t=1}^T p(s_{t+1} \mid s_t, a_t)}_{\text{3. 環境物理轉移 (連乘)}}
\log \pi_\theta(\tau) = \log P(s_0) + \sum_{t=1}^T \log \pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t) + \sum_{t=1}^T \log p(s_{t+1}, r_{t+1} \mid s_t, a_t)
\nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(\tau) = \sum_{t=1}^T \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t)
Put \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(\tau) back into gradient of the estimation of the total reward \nabla_\theta J(\theta)
\nabla_\theta J(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta} \left[ r(\tau) \left( \sum_{t=1}^T \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t) \right) \right]
Gradient ascent
\theta_{t+1} = \theta_t+\alpha \nabla_\theta J(\theta_t)
  
  💡
By the policy gradient theorem, we don’t need to know

Ergodic distribution of states (P)
Environment dynamics (p)

We can still obtain the policy gradient through sampling.
  


Policy gradient theorem


Trajectory level
\nabla_\theta J(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta} \left[ r(\tau) \left( \sum_{t=1}^T \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t) \right) \right]


State-action level
\nabla_\theta J(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta} \left[ Q^{\pi_\theta}(s, a)  \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(s, a) \right]




Derivation of the trajectory level to the state-action level

Monte-Carlo policy gradient (REINFORCE)



Actor-critic policy gradient
Solve the high gradient of REINFORCE → using approximate policy gradient
\begin{aligned}
\nabla_\theta J(\theta) & = \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta} \left[ Q^{\pi_\theta}(s, a)  \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(s, a) \right] \\
& \approx \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta} \left[ Q_w^{\pi_\theta}(s, a)  \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(s, a) \right]
\end{aligned}



Policy gradient method summary

Value-based vs. policy-based vs. actor-critic


value-based: value function approximation


policy-based: policy gradient method

QN vs. DQN
類似但實則不同，難以言傳需意會
QN : 目標是多次sampling然後得到Q的最佳值平均 → minimize 括號內的值

DQN : 目標是直接 minimize 括號內的值(所以也可以用LS)

Deep reinforcement learning algorithm(value approximation, policy gradient)

\mathcal{L}_i(w_i) = \mathbb{E}_{s,a,r,s' \sim D_i} \left[ \left( r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q(s', a'; w_i^-) - Q(s, a; w_i) \right)^2 \right]

off-policy, actor-critic, continuous action

\mathcal{L}(\theta^Q) = \mathbb{E}_{s,a,r,s' \sim D_i} \left[ \left( r + \gamma Q'(s_{t+1}, \mu'(s_{t+1}\vert{}\theta^{\mu'})\vert{}\theta^{Q'}) - Q(s_t, a_t\vert{}\theta^Q) \right)^2 \right]

Techniques/Reinforcement-Learning/策略梯度定理.title: 策略梯度定理推導：從軌跡視角到狀態-動作對視角
Techniques/Reinforcement-Learning/策略梯度定理.content:
📌 核心目標
本筆記旨在推導並證明：策略梯度定理的軌跡視角（Trajectory-level，式一），在數學上如何透過時間因果律與期望值展開，完美轉化為現代 Actor-Critic 常用的狀態-動作對視角（State-Action level，式二）。
🧮 待證明之兩大核心公式


式一：軌跡視角 (Trajectory-level)
\nabla_\theta \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta}[r(\tau)] = \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta} \left[ r(\tau) \left( \sum_{t=1}^T \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t) \right) \right]


式二：狀態-動作對視角 (State-Action level)
\nabla_\theta J(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{s \sim d, a \sim \pi_\theta} \left[ \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(s, a) Q^{\pi_\theta}(s, a) \right]


🛠️ 完整推導步驟

展開式一的內部雙重加總
首先，我們知道一條軌跡 \tau 的總回報 r(\tau) 是各個時間步獎勵的加總，即 r(\tau) = \sum_{k=1}^T r_k。將其帶入式一右側的期望值中：\mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta} \left[ \left( \sum_{k=1}^T r_k \right) \left( \sum_{t=1}^T \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t) \right) \right]
利用代數分配律將這兩個加總（Summation）相乘展開，並根據期望值的線性性質（Linearity of Expectation），將期望值符號 \mathbb{E} 移入第一層加總之內，得到：\sum_{t=1}^T \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta} \left[ \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t) \sum_{k=1}^T r_k \right]
導入時間因果律（Causality）
對於任意特定的時間步 t，我們將總獎勵 \sum_{k=1}^T r_k 拆解為兩部分：過去與當前的獎勵 (k < t)，以及未來的獎勵 (k \ge t)：\sum_{t=1}^T \left( \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta} \left[ \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t) \sum_{k=1}^{t-1} r_k \right] + \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta} \left[ \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t) \sum_{k=t}^T r_k \right] \right)

💡 核心引理 (Causality Lemma)：
在時間步 t之前就已經決定的歷史獎勵 r_k (k < t)，其數值與當前動作的選擇梯度完全獨立。在數學期望值上，過去的獎勵對當前梯度的貢獻恆等於 0。\mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta} \left[ \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t) \sum_{k=1}^{t-1} r_k \right] = 0
因此，上式左半邊的歷史項直接歸零抹去，公式成功簡化為只看當前與未來回報的 Reward-to-go 形式：\sum_{t=1}^T \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta} \left[ \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t) \sum_{k=t}^T r_k \right]

引入 Action-Value Function (Q 函數)
根據馬可夫決策過程（MDP）中，Q 函數的標準微觀定義，它代表「在狀態 s_t 下執行動作 a_t 後，未來預期能拿到的累積折現回報」：Q^{\pi_\theta}(s_t, a_t) = \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta} \left[ \sum_{k=t}^T r_k \;\middle|\; s_t, a_t \right]
利用條件期望式的重複取期望值法則（Law of Total Expectation），我們可以將內部的 Reward-to-go 項直接用 Q 函數替換，將公式改寫為：\sum_{t=1}^T \mathbb{E}_{s_t, a_t \sim \pi_\theta} \left[ \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t) Q^{\pi_\theta}(s_t, a_t) \right]
從時間加總轉換為長期狀態分佈
最後，我們處理最外層對時間步的加總 \sum_{t=1}^T。
智能體在所有時間步 t 所經歷的狀態的平均，在數學上等價於「智能體在長期運行下，訪問到各個狀態的長期狀態訪問頻率（Discounted State Stationary Distribution，通常記為 d(s)）」。\sum_{t=1}^T \mathbb{E}_{s_t \sim \text{環境}} [ \dots ] \equiv \mathbb{E}_{s \sim d} [ \dots ]
因此，我們將時間加總與時間下標 t 移除，正式收攏為整個狀態空間與動作空間的長期期望值形式：\mathbb{E}_{s \sim d, a \sim \pi_\theta} \left[ \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(s, a) Q^{\pi_\theta}(s, a) \right]\

🏁 最終結論
經過上述四個階層的推導，我們成功證明：\nabla_\theta \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\theta}[r(\tau)] = \mathbb{E}_{s \sim d, a \sim \pi_\theta} \left[ \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(s, a) Q^{\pi_\theta}(s, a) \right]
這說明了式一與式二在數學本質上是完全等價的。

式一（REINFORCE）：是以整條軌跡為單位，實作簡單但方差大。
式二（Actor-Critic）：是以單步為單位，透過引進 Q 函數估計，能大幅降低方差，這也是現代 PPO、SAC 演算法更為穩定的數學根基。

Techniques/Robotics/Admittance--and--Imp.title: Admittance & Impedance Control
Techniques/Robotics/Admittance--and--Imp.content:
Overview
Admittance and impedance control are fundamental concepts in robotics and control systems that define how a robot interacts with its environment through force and motion relationships.
Impedance Control
Impedance control regulates the dynamic relationship between force and motion, making the robot behave as a mechanical impedance (mass-spring-damper system).
Key Characteristics

Input: Position/velocity
Output: Force/torque
Behavior: The robot responds to external forces by adjusting its position according to programmed stiffness and damping parameters

Mathematical Representation
The impedance relationship is typically expressed as:
F_{ext} = M\ddot{x} + B\dot{x} + K(x-x_d)
Where:
F_{ext} = applied force
M = desired inertia
B = desired damping
K = desired stiffness
x, ẋ, ẍ = position, velocity, acceleration
x_d = desired position
Using the Jacobian to obtain the extra torque command of each joint:
\tau_{ext} = J^T F_{ext}

Where:
\tau_{ext} = joint torques (n×1 vector)
J^T = transpose of the Jacobian matrix
Admittance Control
Admittance control is the dual of impedance control, regulating the relationship from force to motion, making the robot behave as a mechanical admittance.
Key Characteristics

Input: Force/torque
Output: Position/velocity
Behavior: The robot adjusts its motion in response to measured external forces

Mathematical Representation
The admittance relationship is the inverse (factoring out (1/K)):
\ddot{x} = \frac{1}{M}(F_{ext} - B\dot{x} - K(x-x_d))
Rearranging to make the model output the acceleration \ddot x:
Implementation note: In practice, the controller often computes \ddot x from the measured force (F), then integrates it to get the commanded motion:
\dot{x}(t) = \int \ddot{x}(t) \, dt
x(t) = \int \dot{x}(t) \, dt
Using an iterative method (e.g., Jacobian pseudo-inverse or numerical optimization) to calculate the inverse kinematics and obtain the position command of each joint:
q_{k+1} = q_k + J^{\dagger}(q_k) \cdot (x_d - f(q_k))
Where:
q_k = joint configuration at iteration k
J^{\dagger}(q_k) = pseudo-inverse of the Jacobian matrix at q_k
x_d = desired end-effector position (from admittance model)
f(q_k) = forward kinematics function (current end-effector position)
q_{k+1} = updated joint configuration

Techniques/Robotics/Sensorless-Wrench-Es.content:
Overview
Sensorless wrench estimation is a technique used in robotics to estimate the forces and torques (wrench) applied at the end effector of a robotic manipulator without using dedicated force/torque sensors. This method relies on transforming the torque measurements from the six joints of the robot to calculate the equivalent wrench at the end effector.
Key Concept
The transformation is based on the relationship between joint torques and end effector wrench through the manipulator’s Jacobian matrix. The fundamental equation is:
τ = J^T  F
Where:

τ = Joint torque vector (6×1)
J = Jacobian matrix relating joint velocities to end effector velocities
J^T = Transpose of the Jacobian matrix
F = Wrench at the end effector (6×1 vector: 3 forces + 3 torques)

Estimation Process


Measure joint torques: Obtain torque readings from all six joints using motor current measurements or embedded torque sensors in the joints
τ_{measured} = \begin{bmatrix} τ_1 \\ τ_2 \\ τ_3 \\ τ_4 \\ τ_5 \\ τ_6 \end{bmatrix}


Calculate the Jacobian: Compute the geometric Jacobian matrix based on the current robot configuration (joint angles)
J(q) = \begin{bmatrix} J_{11} & J_{12} & \cdots & J_{16} \\ J_{21} & J_{22} & \cdots & J_{26} \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ J_{61} & J_{62} & \cdots & J_{66} \end{bmatrix}


Compensate for robot dynamics:
τ_{external} = τ_{measured} - τ_{model}
Where τ_{ideal} includes gravity, inertia, and friction effects from the robot dynamics model.
The equation for τ_{ideal}  in robot dynamics is:
τ_{model} = M(q)\ddot{q} + C(q,\dot{q})\dot{q} + G(q) 
Where:

M(q) = Mass/inertia matrix (configuration-dependent)
C(q,ẋ) = Coriolis and centrifugal forces matrix
G(q) = Gravity torque vector
F(ẋ) = Friction torque vector
q = Joint positions
ẋ = Joint velocities
q̈ = Joint accelerations

This represents all the internal torques the robot needs to maintain its motion and counteract gravity and friction, which must be subtracted from the measured torques to isolate external forces.


Solve for external wrench: Subtract gravity and dynamic effects to isolate external forces
F_{external} = (J^T)^{-1} τ_{external}


Advantages

Cost-effective: No need for expensive force/torque sensors
Reduced complexity: Fewer components and wiring
Improved reliability: Fewer sensors mean fewer potential points of failure

Limitations

Accuracy depends on model precision (mass, inertia, friction parameters)
Sensitivity to joint compliance and backlash
Requires accurate knowledge of robot kinematics and dynamics
Performance degrades near singular configurations

CMake
Example file
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.10)
project(MyProject VERSION 1.0.0 LANGUAGES CXX)
 
# 1. Target: Shared Library
add_library(core_logic SHARED 
    src/core.cpp 
    src/utils.cpp
)
 
# 2. Include Directories
target_include_directories(core_logic PUBLIC 
    $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
    $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
)
 
# 3. Compiler Features
target_compile_features(core_logic PUBLIC cxx_std_17)
 
# 4. Target: Executable
add_executable(app_node src/main.cpp)
 
# 5. Linking
target_link_libraries(app_node PRIVATE core_logic)
 
# 6. Installation
install(TARGETS core_logic app_node
    EXPORT MyProjectConfig
    LIBRARY DESTINATION lib
    RUNTIME DESTINATION bin
    ARCHIVE DESTINATION lib
)
🏗️ Core Command Breakdown
cmake_minimum_required()
• Definition: Sets the minimum required CMake version to ensure compatibility with specific features.
• Example: cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.8)
project()
• Definition: Sets the project name, version, and default languages (C, CXX).
• Example: project(example_project)
add_library()
• Definition: Creates a library target from source files.
• Example: add_library(core_logic SHARED src/core.cpp)
add_executable()
• Definition: Creates a binary executable that contains the main() entry point.
• Example: add_executable(app_node src/main.cpp)

⚙️ Target Properties & Logic
target_include_directories()
• Purpose: Tells the compiler where to find .h or .hpp files.
• Scope: PUBLIC means any target linking to this library also gets these headers.
• Example: target_include_directories(core_logic PUBLIC include)
target_compile_features()
• Purpose: Enforces C++ standards (11, 14, 17, 20).
• Example: target_compile_features(core_logic PUBLIC cxx_std_17)

• Purpose: Connects the executable to the library symbols.
